ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ): whoever casts the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl and drops it (قَدَ فْلَحَ), his reasoning is that the hamza, after its vowel was removed, was turned into an alif, and then dropped because it was quiescent and the dāl before it was originally quiescent; and the vowel of the dāl is not taken into account, because it is incidental.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَلَا أَنْسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَا يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (١٠١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): what governs the adverb of time is what governs «بَيْنَهُمْ», namely the omitted element; أَنْسَابَ may not govern it, because the noun of «لَا», when made indeclinable (mabnī), does not govern.

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا وَكُنَّا قَوْمًا ضَالِّينَ (١٠٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (شِقْوَتُنَا): it is read with kasra without an alif, and with fatḥa with an alif (شَقَاوَتُنَا); and they have one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ): the clause is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial), either from the agent or from the object.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا حَتَّى أَنْسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِي وَكُنْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ (١١٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (سِخْرِيًّا): it is a second object. Kasra and ḍamma (سُخْرِيًّا) are two dialectal forms. It is also said: kasra has the meaning of jesting, and ḍamma the meaning of subjugation, from التَّسْخِير; and it is also said: the reverse of that.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ الْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْفَائِزُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنَّهُمْ): it is read with fatḥa, the clause being in the position of a second object, because «جَزَى» takes two objects, as Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً).
There is another view on it, namely that it is with the implied form "because they…" (لِأَنَّهُمْ) or "with the fact that they…" (بِأَنَّهُمْ); i.e. He rewarded them with triumph for their patience. It is also read with kasra (إِنَّهُمْ), as a resumption.

ukberi-tibyan:112-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ (١١٢) قَالُوا لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ فَاسْأَلِ الْعَادِّينَ (١١٣) قَالَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (١١٤) أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُونَ (١١٥))
His saying, the Exalted: (قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ): it is read in the form of the past, i.e. the questioner said to them;
and in the form of the imperative (قُلْ), i.e. Allah says to the questioner: say to them.
(كَمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for لَبِثْتُمْ; i.e. how many years, or the like.
(عَدَدَ): a badal (substitute) from «كَمْ»; it is read anomalously (shādhdh) عَدَدًا, with nunation.
(سِنِينَ): a badal from it.
(الْعَادِّينَ) with doubling, from الْعَدَد ("counting"); and undoubled (الْعَادِينَ) with the meaning of الْعَادِيِّين, i.e. the ancients, as you say "this is an ancient (عَادِيَة) well"; i.e. "ask those who preceded us". One of the two yāʾs of relation (nisba) was dropped, as they said الْأَشْعَرُونَ, and the other was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): i.e. a short time, or a short stay.
The apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْ» is omitted; i.e. "if you had known how long your stay was, you would not have answered with this duration". (عَبَثًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ (١١٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ): like His saying, the Exalted, in al-Baqara: (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ), and it has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ (١١٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ): an adjective (ṣifa) of إِلَه, and the apodosis (jawāb) is «فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ».
His saying: (إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ) is with kasra, as a resumption; and with fatḥa (أَنَّهُ), with the implied form "with the fact that he…" (بِأَنَّهُ); i.e. he is requited with not succeeding. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ (١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَلَقْنَا. (مِنْ طِينٍ): attached to something omitted, because it is an adjective (ṣifa) of سُلَالَة; and it may be attached to the meaning of سُلَالَة, because it has the meaning of مَسْلُولَة ("drawn out").

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَامًا فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ (١٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً): «خَلَقْنَا» has the meaning of "We made into" (صَيَّرْنَا); that is why it takes two objects in the accusative.
(الْعِظَامَ): in the plural, according to the original, and in the singular (الْعَظْمَ), because it is a genus.
(أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ): a badal (substitute), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); it is not an adjective (ṣifa), because it is indefinite even though it is put in construct, since the muḍāf ilayhi stands in place of «مِنْ»; and so it is with the whole category of «أَفْعَلُ مِنْكَ» (the comparative).

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ (١٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ): what governs it is «مَيِّتُونَ», and the lām here does not prevent the governing.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّا عَلَى ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ (١٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذَهَاب. And «عَلَى» is attached to «قَادِرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ (٢٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَشَجَرَةً): i.e. "and We produced a tree"; so it is conjoined to «جَنَّاتٍ».
(سَيْنَاءَ): it is read with kasra on the sīn (سِينَاءَ); on this reading the hamza is a radical, like حِمْلَاق, and it is not for the feminine, since there is nothing in the language like سَنَا - سَيَا [Translator's note: so in the source; the point is that no root exists from which a feminine pattern fiʿlāʾ could be formed here]. It is a diptote because it is the name of a tract of land, so it has definiteness and femininity; and it may also have foreignness (ʿujma).
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn; on this reading the hamza is for the feminine, since there is no faʿlāl pattern with fatḥa in the language. What al-Farrāʾ reported of their saying "a she-camel in which there is خَزْعَال (lameness)" is not established, and if it were established it would be anomalous (shādhdh) and nothing would be based on it.
His saying, the Exalted: (تَنْبُتُ): it is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ (تُنْبِتُ), and there are two views on it. First: it is transitive, and the object is omitted, its implied form being "it produces its fruit" or "its harvest"; on this view the bāʾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what is omitted, i.e. "with oil in it", as you say "Zayd went out with his clothes". It is also said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), so there is then no omission; rather, the object is الدُّهْن. The second view: it is intransitive; one says نَبَتَ الْبَقْلُ and أَنْبَتَ with the same meaning; on this view the bāʾ is a ḥāl. It is also said: it is an object; i.e. it grows because of the oil.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the bāʾ (تُنْبَتُ), and that is clear.
It is also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ (تَنْبُتُ), and it is like the second view mentioned.
(وَصِبْغٍ): conjoined to الدُّهْن.
It has been read, among the anomalous readings, in the accusative (وَصِبْغًا), conjoined to the position of بِالدُّهْنِ.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (نُسْقِيكُمْ): it is read with nūn, and this has been mentioned in al-Naḥl; and with tāʾ (تُسْقِيكُمْ), in which case it contains the pronoun of the livestock, and it is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ فَاسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِنَّهُمْ مُغْرَقُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِأَعْيُنِنَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. guarded.
(مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): has been mentioned in Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:29-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَنْزِلْنِي مُنْزَلًا مُبَارَكًا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ (٢٩) إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ (٣٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مُنْزَلًا): it is read with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the zāy (مَنْزِلًا); it is a place, or the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نَزَلَ [Translator's note: the source prints نَزَّلَ], which is the reflexive-compliant (muṭāwiʿ) of أَنْزَلْتُهُ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the zāy (مُنْزَلًا), and it is a maṣdar with the meaning of الْإِنْزَال; it may also be a place, as you say "I set down at the place", so it is مُنْزَل.
(وَإِنْ كُنَّا): i.e. "indeed we were"; so it is lightened from the heavy (inna), and this has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مُتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ): concerning the iʿrāb of this verse there are several views:
The first: that the noun of the first «أَنَّ» is omitted (a muḍāf), with the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, its implied form being "that your being brought out…" (أَنَّ إِخْرَاجَكُمْ); and «إِذَا» is the khabar (predicate); and «أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ» is a repetition, because «أَنَّ» with what it governs is for emphasis, or to indicate what is omitted. The second: that the noun of «أَنَّ» is the kāf and mīm, and «إِذَا» is conditional, its apodosis (jawāb) being omitted, its implied form being "that you, when you die, it will come about that you are brought out"; so the second أَنَّكُمْ with what it governs is the fāʿil (agent) of the apodosis of إِذَا, and the whole clause is the khabar of the first أَنَّ. The third: that the khabar of the first is مُخْرَجُونَ, and the second أَنَّ is repeated alone for emphasis; that is permissible when the speech has become long, just as it is permissible with the kasra form in His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا) and (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السُّوءَ); this has been mentioned in al-Naḥl. The fourth: that the khabar of the first «أَنَّ» is omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it. «إِذَا» cannot be the khabar of the first (on this view), because it is an adverb of time and its noun denotes a concrete entity (juththa). As for what governs «إِذَا», it is omitted: on the first view the implied element is (a word) of settledness (al-istiqrār); on the second view it is governed by its omitted apodosis; and on the third and fourth it is governed by what the khabar of the second indicates. «مُتُّمْ» does not govern it, because it (إِذَا) is put in construct with it.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هَيْهَاتَ): it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), a statement standing in the place of بَعُدَ ("it is far"). Concerning its fāʿil (agent) there are two views. First: it is latent, its implied form being "far is the belief in what you are promised", or "its truth", or "its occurrence", and the like. Second: its fāʿil is «مَا», and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); i.e. "far is what you are promised of the resurrection".
Some said: «هَيْهَاتَ» has the meaning of الْبُعْد ("farness"), so its position is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ» is the khabar (predicate); this is weak. On the first view «هَيْهَاتَ» has no grammatical position. There are several readings of it: fatḥa without nunation, as being singular; with nunation, intending intensification; kasra without nunation, and with nunation, as being a feminine plural; and ḍamma in both ways, likened to قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ.
It is also read هَيْهَاهْ, with hāʾ, both in pause and in connected speech.
It is also read أَيْهَاهْ, with hamza substituted for the first hāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نَادِمِينَ (٤٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ): «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida).
It is also said: it has the meaning of "a thing" or "a time". It is also said: (قَلِيلٍ is) a badal (substitute) from it.
In the speech there is an omitted oath, whose answer is «لَيُصْبِحُنَّ».
«عَنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُصْبِحُنَّ; the lām did not prevent this as the lām of the mubtadaʾ (lām al-ibtidāʾ) prevents it. They permitted زَيْدٌ لَأَضْرِبَنَّ ("Zayd, I shall surely strike"), because the lām is for emphasis, so it is like قَدْ, and like the lām of emphasis in the khabar of إِنَّ, as in His saying: (بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ).
It is also said: the lām here prevents fronting except with adverbs, for latitude is allowed with them.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى كُلَّمَا جَاءَ أُمَّةً رَسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ فَأَتْبَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ بَعْضًا وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ فَبُعْدًا لِقَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (تَتْرَى): the tāʾ is a substitute for wāw, because it is from الْمُوَاتَرَة, which is succession; that is from their saying "they came in one وَتِيرَة", i.e. in one manner. It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in succession; strictly speaking it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. It is also said: it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a successive sending".
Concerning its alif there are three views. First: it is for attachment (ilḥāq) to the pattern of جَعْفَر, like the alif in أَرْطَى; that is why it takes nunation [Translator's note: the printed text has تُؤَنَّثُ ("is made feminine"); تُنَوَّنُ ("takes nunation") is evidently intended, matching the third view] according to those who treat it as fully declinable. Second: it is a substitute for nunation. Third: it is for the feminine, like سَكْرَى; that is why it does not take nunation according to those who treat it as a diptote.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَى وَأَخَاهُ هَارُونَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ (٤٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هَارُونَ): it is a badal (substitute) from «أَخَاهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَابِدُونَ (٤٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِثْلِنَا): it was not put in the dual only because «مِثْل» has the status of a maṣdar (verbal noun); its dual and plural do occur, in His saying (يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ) and in His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ).
It is also said: it was kept singular only because what is meant is likeness in humanity, not quantity.
It is also said: the singular sufficed in place of the dual.

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ (٥) إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ (٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ): in the position of the accusative, governed by «حَافِظُونَ» according to the meaning, because the meaning is: they guarded them from every private part except from the private parts of their spouses.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. they guarded them in every state except in this state.
It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مَلُومِينَ», for two reasons: first, what comes after «إِنَّ» does not govern what precedes it; second, the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes it.
«عَلَى» is attached to حَافِظُونَ only according to the meaning; and it may be attached to a verb indicated by «مَلُومِينَ», i.e. "except with their spouses they are not blamed".

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلْنَا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إِلَى رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ (٥٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً): has been mentioned in al-Anbiyāʾ.
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمَعِينٍ): there are two views on it. First: it is of the pattern faʿīl from الْمَعْن, which is a small thing; and from it is الْمَاعُون. It is also said: الْمَاعُون is water; so the mīm is a radical. Second: the mīm is augmentative, and it is from عِنْتُهُ, "I saw it with my eye"; its original form is مَعْيُون.

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاتَّقُونِ (٥٢) فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًا كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ (٥٣))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza (وَأَنَّ), and there are three views on it. First: its implied form is "and because…", the implied lām being attached (mutaʿalliq) to «فَاتَّقُونِ», i.e. "so fear Me, because this…". The position of أَنَّ is accusative, or genitive, according to the disagreement we have reported in more than one place. Second: it is conjoined to what precedes it, its implied form being "I am Knowing of what you do, and of the fact that this…". Third: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and know that this…".
It is also read with the nūn undoubled (وَأَنْ), and it is lightened from the heavy (anna).
It is also read with kasra, as a resumption.
(أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً): has been mentioned in al-Anbiyāʾ, as has «فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ». (زُبُرًا), with two ḍammas, is the plural of زَبُور, like رَسُول and رُسُل.
It is also read with the bāʾ quiescent (زُبْرًا), with this meaning.
It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ (زُبَرًا), and it is the plural of زُبْرَة, which is a piece or a party. The accusative on the first view is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَمْرَهُمْ», i.e. like books. It is also said: from the agent pronoun. It is also said: it is a second object of تَقَطَّعُوا. On the second view, it is a ḥāl from the agent.

ukberi-tibyan:55-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ (٥٥) نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ بَل لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٥٦))
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنَّمَا): (مَا) has the meaning of الَّذِي, and the khabar (predicate) of أَنَّ is «نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ», with the returning pronoun omitted; i.e. "We hasten for them in it". The khabar may not be «مِنْ مَالٍ», because if it were «مِنْ مَالٍ», that would not be held against them; what is held against them is only their belief that those riches are good for them.
نُسَارِعُ is also read with yāʾ and with nūn, and with the agent unnamed, and نُسْرِعُ without an alif.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ رَاجِعُونَ (٦٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَا آتَوْا): «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, and the returning pronoun is omitted; i.e. "they give what they give".
It is also read: أَتَوْا, without prolongation; i.e. "what they came to (do)".
(أَنَّهُمْ…): i.e. "fearful of their returning to their Lord"; so the preposition was dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَهُمْ لَهَا): i.e. "for their sake". It is also said: the implied form is "and they race them", i.e. they hasten to them; so it is in the position of the object. The like of it is (هُمْ لَهَا عَامِلُونَ), i.e. for its sake, and it is what they do.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذْنَا مُتْرَفِيهِمْ بِالْعَذَابِ إِذَا هُمْ يَجْأَرُونَ (٦٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِذَا): it is of surprise (mufājaʾa), and its rule has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:66-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ كَانَتْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ تَنْكِصُونَ (٦٦) مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ سَامِرًا تَهْجُرُونَ (٦٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «تَنْكِصُونَ»; and His saying, the Exalted, «مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ» is another ḥāl.
The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to the Mighty Qurʾān. It is also said: to the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace. It is also said: to the command of Allah the Exalted. It is also said: to the House; on this view it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سَامِرًا», i.e. "you hold night talk around the House".
It is also said: (attached) to the Qurʾān. سَامِرًا is also a ḥāl, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in their saying قُمْ قَائِمًا ("stand up standing"); maṣdars do occur in the form of the active participle, such as الْعَاقِبَة and الْعَافِيَة. It is also said: it is a singular in the place of a plural.
It has also been read: (سُمَّرًا), the plural of سَامِر, like شَاهِد and شُهَّد.
(تَهْجُرُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in سَامِرًا. It is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, from your saying هَجَرَ يَهْجُرُ, when one talks nonsense. It is also said: they forsake the Qurʾān.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm (تُهْجِرُونَ), from أَهْجَرَ, when one utters الْهُجْر, which is obscenity. It is also read with doubling (تُهَجِّرُونَ), and it has the meaning of the undoubled form. Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ خَرْجًا فَخَرَاجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ (٧٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (خَرْجًا): it is read without an alif in the first and with an alif in the second.
It is also read without an alif in both, and with an alif in both; and they have the same meaning.
It is also said: الْخَرْج is the wage, and الْخَرَاج is what is levied on land and on persons.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ (٧٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نَاكِبُونَ», and the lām does not prevent that.

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِالْعَذَابِ فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ (٧٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا): has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān, together with the disagreement about it.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ (٧٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ): has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:84-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ وَمَنْ فِيهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٨٤) سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٨٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ): the first occurrence is with the lām in the reading of the majority; it is the answer to what contains the lām, namely His saying, the Exalted: (لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ), and it matches both wording and meaning.
It has also been read without the lām (اللَّهُ), construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ» is "who is the Lord of the earth?", so the answer is "Allah", i.e. "He is Allah".
As for the other two occurrences, they are read without the lām, construed according to the wording, being the answer to His saying, the Exalted: (مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ); and «مَنْ بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ» (is answered) with the lām according to the meaning, because the meaning of His saying «مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ» is "to whom do the heavens belong?". [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the source; it describes the reading without lām in the last two answers (vv. 87, 89) and the majority reading with lām (لِلَّهِ) construed by meaning.]

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ (٨) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَى صَلَوَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ (٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ): it is read in the plural, because they are many, as in His saying, the Exalted: (أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا); and in the singular (لِأَمَانَتِهِمْ), because it is a genus, so in being singular it is like عَهْدِهِمْ. The like of it is (صَلَوَاتِهِمْ), in the singular and the plural.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (٩٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ): it is read in the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute) of the name of Allah the Exalted before it; and in the nominative (عَالِمُ), i.e. "He is the Knower".

ukberi-tibyan:94-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي فِي الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ (٩٤) وَإِنَّا عَلَى أَنْ نُرِيَكَ مَا نَعِدُهُمْ لَقَادِرُونَ (٩٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي): the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, namely His saying, the Exalted: (إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي), and the vocative is parenthetical between them. (عَلَى): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قَادِرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ (٩٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ارْجِعُونِ): there are three views on it. First: it is put in the plural for majesty, as Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ), and as in His saying, the Exalted: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا). Second: he meant "O angels of my Lord, send me back". Third: by the plural form he indicated repetition of the saying, as though he said "send me back, send me back".
